title: PDL Week 7
coldOpen:
Both undefeated teams went down, Brett has requested formal recognition for his winning streak, and Greg insists selling half his roster before Halloween isn't tilting. 

Welcome to Week 6 of the PDL Power Rankings.

1: I had already accepted the loss to Mike before Sunday even started.
Lamar was out, Hurts was out, Tyler Warren was unavailable, and Josh Jacobs was making sure those tapes stayed sealed.
My two starting quarterbacks were Tyler Shough and Tyler Huntley.
I was preparing to face one of the best teams in the PDL with a quarterback room that sounded like the first two names called during attendance at a BYU orientation.
And somehow, Delco won. 136.26 to 126.16.
Mike is no longer undefeated.
Shough threw for 144 yards against the Giants and somehow accounted for FOUR touchdowns, finishing with 32.96 points.
DeVonta returned with 17, Metcalf had a productive afternoon, and even Chig decided to help out while Warren was sidelined.
I spent the entire offseason preparing for a future without Lamar and Hurts, and apparently the first step of that transition was to accidentally beat Southern Oregon with two guys named Tyler.
Naturally, I was pretty excited about this.
We had just knocked off one of the league's two remaining undefeated teams; I finally had something to hold over Mike, and the roster was beginning to show signs of life.
I even considered writing a paragraph about how everyone underestimated Delco, but I figured nobody deserved to read that.
I didn't even get to enjoy this because of news that Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the season after doctors discovered blood clots in his lungs.
That one genuinely sucks.
I've spent years listening to people argue about Hurts, whether he's an elite quarterback, how much of his success is attributable to the supporting cast, whether the Eagles should move on.
I would give quite a bit to spend the next few months being annoyed by those conversations instead of wondering what this team is supposed to look like without him.
His prognosis is reportedly very good, and I hope we see him healthy and back on the field next year.

So, yes, even when Delco wins, I somehow come out of the weekend considerably more depressed about football than when it started because you have to remember, I'm a football fan first, fantasy fan second.
There are some actual reasons to be optimistic about this roster, though.
Jacobs has finally been removed from the commissioner's exempt list and is eligible to return.
Lamar is getting closer, Shough has been genuinely good, and Smitty looks healthy again.
I may actually have enough functioning players to stop treating the weekly injury report like my primary source of roster construction.
And then there's Mope..Mini Va...MITSUBISHI MARV!
I spent approximately six paragraphs last week defending Marv, celebrating his escape from Arizona, and explaining why Houston was finally going to give him the opportunity he deserved.
His Texans debut? Three catches, 34 yards, and 4.90 fantasy points.
The fantasy stats don't look impressive, but his usage when he was actually on the field was glorious.
Still, we're 3-3, Mike has a loss, and for the first time in a while I can look at my roster and reasonably expect it to improve over the next few weeks.
That's about as much optimism as I'm comfortable expressing in writing.
I've already lost one quarterback for the year, and I'd prefer to get through Tuesday before making any more declarations about this team's future.
2: I owe Max an apology.
Last week I moved him below a 1-4 Hollywood team after he beat Connecticut with 74.72 points.
I assumed that was a Max problem.
Then Welch rolled in fresh off a 162-point performance against Greg, scored 81.64, and still won by forty.
I'm beginning to suspect Joe is doing something to these people.
Look at the last two weeks.

Max scored 143.24 against Darren before facing Joe. 
Welch scored 162.28 against London.
Those same two teams proceeded to score a COMBINED 156.36 against Connecticut.
Tanish scored 197.72 by himself last week.
What exactly happens when these owners see Joe on their schedule?
Do they stop setting alarms?
Is everyone just agreeing beforehand that this thing doesn't need to get competitive?
And Joe is having a perfectly lovely time.
Tanner McKee was his leading scorer this week, Kaleb Johnson managed to lose two yards on his only carry, and Malik Benson contributed absolutely nothing.
Meanwhile, Welch now has to explain how the roster I was just discussing as a potential championship contender barely cracked 80 points.
Remember, the PDL's sixth playoff spot is determined by points scored.
Imagine being in a tight race for that final spot, seeing Connecticut on your schedule, and thinking you're about to pad your season total.
Instead, you get an 81-point win and spend Tuesday having your entire roster questioned by the guy who writes these rankings.
Joe has somehow found a way to lose every game while making the winners look increasingly sus.
There's genuinely no good outcome when you play him.
You either become the first person to lose to Connecticut, in which case I recommend leaving the league, or you win, and I start asking why you couldn't score 100.
Max, I was too hard on you last week. Welch, I guess you're gonna have to wait until you get to your write-up.
3: Jeff finally lost a football game, and I have a feeling he's considerably more upset about what happened in Los Angeles than anything Darren did to him.
Sean McVay announced Monday that Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring against Arizona and is expected to miss six to ten weeks.
We're six weeks into the NFL season, and Jeff may have just lost his best receiver until the fantasy playoffs.
I imagine whatever frustration he had about losing to Darren by 2.50 points became considerably less important once that news came out.
The frustrating thing about Wichita is that even when things go wrong, you still have to play a pretty excellent game to beat them.
Mahomes finished with 9.48 points, Derrick Henry lost a fumble and contributed 4.50, and Jeff's three starting receivers combined for 19.30.
Somehow, Kenneth Walker, McCaffrey and James Cook still managed to produce 75.90 points between them.
Aaron Rodgers also had to cover for Patrick Mahomes, which is an interesting sentence to be writing in October 2026.
And Darren STILL only won by 2.50.
I'm not particularly interested in criticizing Jeff's lineup decisions, although Tre Tucker putting up 24.20 points on the bench certainly hurts in hindsight.
The bigger concern is what happens to this receiving room now. A.J. Brown finally returned and caught three of TEN targets for 27 yards.
Courtland Sutton contributed 2.90 points, Deebo remains unavailable, and Adams is looking at a recovery timetable that could stretch into late December.
Tucker's 97-yard, two-touchdown performance against Buffalo might end up being considerably more important than anyone expected.
For all the attention we've given Jeff's running backs and quarterbacks, I'm beginning to wonder whether his receiving room is going to be the thing that determines how far this team actually goes.
He's assembled enough talent elsewhere that I still think Wichita can survive the injury, but replacing Adams' production for potentially the next two months is a legitimate problem.
Losing out on the Tee Higgins sweepstakes may haunt Wichita even more.
As for the ranking, I'm leaving Jeff at #1.
He's 5-1, still holds the league's highest scoring average, and just came within a field goal of beating one of the PDL's strongest teams despite getting very little from several important starters.
Tanish has made this a considerably more difficult decision than it was two weeks ago, but I don't think one narrow loss warrants moving Wichita out of the top spot.
I will say that Darren has earned the right to be insufferable about this one.
He spent the past month listening to us discuss whether anyone could realistically challenge Wichita, then went out and beat him with Jahmyr Gibbs on bye.
Jeff, if it's any consolation, you can probably avoid the podcast for a week and never hear about the loss again.
I'm sure Darren will be perfectly reasonable about it.
The Adams news, unfortunately, is going to be a little harder to ignore.
4: Max scored 144.42 points this week, finishing just 1.08 behind Tanish for the highest score in the PDL.
Ja'Marr Chase was on his bye.
Ladd McConkey gave him 2.2 points.

At some point, we're going to have to discuss how the guy who started selling off his roster in September has somehow won three consecutive games and is now beating teams that actually intended to compete this season.
I want it on the record that I've been an MSE believer.
I'm also beginning to think the Dak trade worked out better than many other PDL guys may want to believe.
Bryce Young and C.J. Stroud combined for 51.82 points this week, with Bryce leading Carolina over Philly and Stroud winning a shootout in London.
As an Eagles fan, watching Bryce Young throw two touchdowns to Tommy Tremble was already an upsetting experience.
Finding out that Max owns BOTH but had Tremble on the bench, made it sting less.
Tremble actually scored 20.60 points, where he was sitting behind Kyle Pitts, who ALSO caught two touchdowns against Chicago.
Four touchdowns from two tight ends. Max managed to benefit from the Eagles' loss twice without even starting both players.
And Tennessee finally won a football game!
Carnell Tate caught his first NFL touchdown, helping the Titans overcome a 13-point deficit against Indianapolis.
The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard the following morning.
After six weeks, Max's investment in Tennessee has finally produced something of significance, even if that significance is mostly unemployment in Indianapolis.
Cam Ward, meanwhile, finished with 7.78 points on Max's bench.
Bryce Young alone outscored the entire Ward/Tate stack by 0.06. I think we can safely leave that particular experiment alone for a while.
The interesting development for MSE is how much more functional this receiving room is becoming.
Coker has emerged as a legitimate contributor, Tate is beginning to justify his draft capital, and even Romeo Doubs continues to find ways to be useful (Darren in shambles).
Chase returns next week, and Max suddenly has enough options that he doesn't need every single one of them to produce to remain competitive.
I still want to see him address the running backs.
Jordan Mason remains on IR, Monangai is hurt, and I don't particularly trust a long-term combination of Woody Marks and Rachaad White.
Max is averaging 115.2 points per game, so one excellent week doesn't erase some of the uglier performances we've already witnessed.
But the same roster we were questioning three weeks ago just beat Hollywood without its best player, put up the second-highest score of the week, and improved to 4-2.
Ja'Marr Chase comes back next week. It's getting exciting.
5: Jon finally got a legitimate breakout performance from one of his 2026 first-round picks this weekend.
Omar Cooper missed five weeks, returned with 103 yards and a touchdown, and Jon left him on the bench while his three starting receivers combined for 12.80 points.
His Sleeper username is BitConfusedJon. I'm beginning to appreciate the transparency.
He finished with 19.30 fantasy points, which would've made him Richmond's highest-scoring player.
The three rookie receivers he actually started, Makai Lemon, Antonio Williams and Malachi Fields, combined for 12.80 points.
Still, I think there's some encouraging stuff happening here.
Mason Taylor has become a pretty reliable tight end, Sadiq returned from his concussion, and Cooper looked fantastic in his first meaningful action since September.
The Jets have now had breakout performances from three different first-round rookies this season.
Unfortunately, they're still the Jets, and Aaron Glenn's team has somehow been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of first halves during his tenure.
Six points across 23 games. I'm genuinely curious whether Glenn has considered just kneeling out the remainder of the second quarter regardless of field position.
There was also a brief moment Sunday when Jon's starting quarterback, Jalon Daniels, appeared to be orchestrating a pretty significant upset against Pittsburgh.
Tampa entered the fourth quarter leading 16-3 before Old Man Rodgers decided he'd seen enough and brought the Steelers back to win in overtime.
Daniels finished with two interceptions, and Jon subsequently lost to Tanish by 85.84 points.
This is what Jon gets for skipping the Pittsburgh Draft trip; having a 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers personally intervene in your afternoon seems excessive.
We are now entering week 7, and Jon has to feel the temperatures rising a bit.
He doesn't have Joe's collection of 2027 firsts waiting to rescue him.
He's got four seconds next year, with his next first-round capital arriving in 2028.
Lemon, Sadiq, Cooper, Williams, Fields and the rest of this rookie class are the players he needs to build around.
Some are starting to show why he drafted them, though getting them all healthy and productive at the same time remains a difficult ask.
I wouldn't be surprised if Jon eventually looks back on this season pretty favorably despite the record.
He just needs a few more Sundays like Cooper's, preferably with the points going somewhere other than his bench.
6: Apparently, one of the more popular opinions on the podcast is that Hollywood has a better team than Delco.
I don't even have a good rebuttal because I spent last week defending Brian myself.
He scored 142.60 against Mike, I moved him ahead of Max despite Max actually winning his matchup, and then those two played each other this week.
I would've liked to enjoy my editorial decision for at least seven days before looking like an idiot.
Hollywood has now lost five straight games, which is getting harder to understand with how talented this roster is.

Tuten is turning into a terrific investment, Egbuka continues to produce, and Brian has somehow assembled a quarterback room where Michael Penix can throw three touchdowns against Chicago, and it barely warrants a discussion about changing his starters.
Jordan Love and Kirk Cousins were both perfectly reasonable plays this week.
The Tee Higgins acquisition was interesting, too.

Brian sent Jayden Noel and his 2028 first to Greg, who's been running London's liquidation sale with the urgency of someone fleeing the country (with the midterms going on right now, I wanna flee too).
Higgins immediately went on bye, Jeremiyah Love was unavailable, and Brian ended up starting MarShawn Lloyd in his flex for one point.
At least he's getting an early opportunity to experience what his expensive new receiving room looks like without its expensive new receiver.
I don't think 126 points is necessarily a bad performance, and that's what makes ranking Hollywood frustrating.

His 122-point weekly average is actually higher than Max's 115.2, despite Max now sitting at 4-2. Brian has enough young talent that I wouldn't be surprised to see him put together an excellent second half of the season, especially once Love returns and Higgins gets settled.
The sixth playoff spot being determined by points scored also means his record hasn't entirely killed him yet.
However, I would appreciate it if everyone could stop describing Hollywood's eventual fully healthy roster as though it's the team Brian has been putting on the field every Sunday.
He gets the 5-1 Boulder Bears next week, by the way.
I look forward to hearing why Hollywood is better than Delco at 1-6.
7: I had Darren at #3 when I first started putting these rankings together.
Then I imagined spending the next 48 hours defending my decision to move my podcast co-host up, so I quietly put him back at #4.
I am somehow being bullied by a group chat that hasn't even seen the rankings yet.
Anyway, THE UNDEFEATED STREAK IS OVER.
Darren handed Jeff his first loss of the season, winning 140.00 to 137.50, and with Delco upsetting Mike on the same weekend, we officially have no undefeated teams remaining in the PDL.
I'd like to thank Darren for doing his part, although I would have appreciated this performance a week earlier when Jeff was beating me by 53 with half the Chiefs on bye.
What makes Philadelphia's win particularly impressive is how little help Darren received from some of his biggest names.
Gibbs was on bye, Darnold finished with nine points, Garrett Wilson contributed 6.40, and CeeDee Lamb needed EIGHTEEN targets to finish with 70 yards.
I genuinely don't understand how Dallas manages to make throwing the ball to CeeDee Lamb look like such an exhausting process.
Darren still won.
Swift continued his productive season, Stafford held things together, Golden had another strong performance, and George Kittle picked a pretty good time to return to the end zone.
Gemie Bernard and Luther Burden also combined for 33.70 points on the bench.
Darren is going to be absolutely insufferable when he realizes he can start bragging about his young receivers soon.
Last week he scored 174.82 and lost to Tanish.
This week he scored 140 and knocked off the team we've spent the past month calling the best in the league.
That's 314.82 points over two weeks against the two teams currently sitting at 5-1.
At some point, I'm going to need everyone to explain what exactly they're seeing that makes moving Philadelphia into the top three such an outrageous proposition.
And I think Darren knows it.

The man has spent years cultivating his reputation as the PDL's villain, handing out unsolicited roster evaluations on the podcast, and generally making sure nobody enjoys beating him more than they should.
Well, he just beat the league's biggest spender while leaving the RB1 on bye.
He gets Welch next week, who is coming off an 81-point performance against Connecticut.
I'm sure Darren has already begun preparing the show doc for next week.
8: Last week I asked whether Welch finally had the roster to compete with Mike and Jeff.
His response was to score 81.64 points against Joe.
I know Jared Goff and Amon-Ra were on bye, but I didn't realize the Detroit Lions were responsible for approximately half of Dallas's entire offense.
This was an alarming performance from a team with legitimate championship aspirations.
Dak followed up last week's disaster with another two-interception outing against Green Bay, Jacoby Brissett contributed 5.92 points, and Juwan Johnson managed a zero.
Welch's two starting quarterbacks combined for 16.94 points.
Tyler Shough scored nearly twice that by himself.
Lineup management wasn't even the issue here.
McCarthy scored 17.32 on the bench, and Demario Douglas had another productive afternoon with 16.10.
Even if Welch had started both over Brissett and McLaurin, Dallas would've finished with 105.94 points.
Better, sure, but still nowhere near the kind of performance we've come to expect from a team averaging nearly 137 points per game.
I spent a good portion of last week's entry discussing how much I liked this roster, and I still do.
Watson, London and Amon-Ra give Welch a terrific receiving trio, McBride remains one of the best tight ends in fantasy, and Goff has been excellent.
But I'm becoming concerned about how much of this team's weekly ceiling depends on Detroit.
You're going to need something more reliable out of the other quarterback spot, and the running back situation isn't particularly reassuring either.
Irving struggled, Montgomery was unavailable, and Harvey was left trying to keep things respectable while Conner and Benson remain on IR.
The bright side is that Welch walked away with a win and improved to 4-2.

He also remains firmly in the playoff conversation, although I'm not sure how much comfort I'd take from beating Connecticut when literally every other team in the league scored more than you this week.
Next up is Darren, who just handed Jeff his first loss of the season.
Goff and Amon-Ra will be back, which is fortunate because I suspect Darren will require slightly more than 81 points to beat.
Welch has spent years trying to get over the hump in the PDL.
I'd prefer we didn't discover halfway through his supposed championship season that the entire operation hinges on the Lions never having an off week.
9: I think we owe Mike an apology.
We've spent years calling him the PDL's resident tilter, but I have some evidence pointing that it is another PDL member.

A man who spent an entire offseason acquiring running backs like they were property on an oil field, submitted something like 46 offers trying to land Rome Odunze, and then got FOUR WEEKS into the season before deciding he'd seen enough.
He insists he isn't tilting. Okay, Greg.
I genuinely want to understand the thought process here.
London was 2-2, had just put up 140 points against Jeff, and Greg's response was to sell Jeff Derrick Henry.
The same Henry he acquired not too long ago for a run.
We hadn't even reached the halfway point of the fantasy season, and Greg was already making decisions for 2028.
We don't even know what half these teams are going to look like come playoff time.
And can we revisit the Rome trade for a moment?
We spent weeks trying to justify what was widely considered one of the worst trades in recent PDL history because of how badly Greg wanted Odunze.
Fine.
Sometimes you pay a premium to get your guy.
But that argument becomes considerably harder to defend when you immediately abandon the entire competitive window you acquired him for.
Olave is now helping Mike, Henry and Sutton are helping Jeff, Higgins is in Hollywood, and Greg is sitting at home with a bunch of future picks and the satisfaction of knowing he finally has Rome.
I guess we are playing for different objectives here?
Speaking of which, London lost to Brett this week, 112.54 to 86.76.
Odunze contributed 5.40 points while Jayden Noel, the receiver Greg got back in the Higgins trade, was London's highest scorer with 18.70.
He also managed to leave Tyrone Tracy and Blake Corum on the bench, who combined for 30.50 points.
For someone who spent the offseason collecting running backs, Greg has somehow arrived at a situation where he has too many to start and apparently not enough to keep.
I understand the argument for selling aging assets, and two additional 2028 firsts could eventually be worth quite a bit.
But I'd be more sympathetic if we weren't discussing a team that was being assembled to contend approximately fifteen minutes ago.

Even after this week's disaster, London is averaging 115.6 points per game, nearly twenty more than the Brett team that just beat him. The roster wasn't nearly as hopeless as Greg appears to have decided it was.
He's now lost three straight, dropped to 2-4.

I'm sorry, but you don't get to spend an entire offseason convincing everyone you're building a championship contender, abandon the project before Halloween, and then act surprised when people accuse you of tilting.
I'd love for Greg to come back on the podcast and explain this.
We haven't heard from him in weeks, and I have several follow-up questions.
Mike, if you're reading this, I owe you an apology.
You might not even be the biggest tilter in your own division anymore.
As for Greggy; I doubt he has even read this far.
10: Mike has spent the past several weeks making a pretty convincing argument that he deserves to reclaim the top spot in these rankings.
All he needed was for Jeff to finally lose a game.
Well, Darren took care of that Sunday, and Mike responded by losing to the Delco Dreamers.
The timing genuinely could not have worked out better for me.
I've been extremely mature about this, as I'm sure everyone can attest.
In fairness, Southern Oregon was missing quite a bit this week.
Justin Jefferson and Sam LaPorta were on bye, the Miami running backs Mike acquired from Max were unavailable, Achane remains on IR, and Charbonnet is still on PUP.
He nevertheless got 65.56 combined points from Josh Allen, Brock Purdy and Isaiah Likely, which ordinarily should be a pretty comfortable starting point.
Unfortunately, none of his five starting receivers managed to score more than Olave's 12.30, and Kenneth Gainwell was apparently the answer to his RB2 situation.
I think that's the one area Mike needs to seriously consider addressing before the trade deadline.
Jeanty continues to be an interesting fantasy player, but he just finished with 22 rushing yards on 10 carries and needed his receiving work and a touchdown to salvage 13.80 points.
Gainwell contributed 2.90.
Mike has spent much of the season assembling solutions to his running back situation, and we're six weeks in with the position still looking pretty uncomfortable whenever someone is unavailable.
I'm not particularly convinced that hoping Miami eventually has two functioning running backs is a championship strategy.
The funny thing is that Mike's disappointing week was still good for 126.16 points.
That's more than half the league managed to score.
Hollywood would've lost to him by a tenth of a point.
I'm keeping Southern Oregon at #2 because I still think the healthy version of this roster is among the best in the league.
Jefferson returns, LaPorta returns, Puka remains excellent, and Mike has enough quarterback and receiving talent to beat virtually anyone.
Tanish is certainly making a case to move ahead of him, though, especially after leading the league in scoring for two consecutive weeks.
With all three teams at 5-1, the margin between the top spots is getting awfully thin.
11: Brett specifically requested that I acknowledge Dubrovnik's three-game winning streak in this week's rankings, and I'm happy to oblige.
The Dragons have won THREE consecutive games, climbed back to .500, and are officially one of the hottest teams in the PDL.
Their three opponents were Brian, Jon, and Greg, who currently have a combined record of 3-15.
Brett, I can only do so much here.
Now, I actually think there's a pretty good argument that Dubrovnik is heading in the right direction.
Trevor Lawrence has become QB7, Tetairoa McMillan looks every bit the receiver Brett hoped he was getting, and Colston Loveland finally had the kind of game we've been waiting for.
Caleb Williams returned against Atlanta and immediately remembered he has a very talented tight end, connecting with Loveland for six catches, 65 yards, and his first touchdown of the season.
Between him and Tucker Kraft, Brett is starting to develop a pretty formidable TE room.
Trevor also threw four touchdowns against Houston in London, finishing with 34.34 fantasy points.
Jacksonville somehow lost that game despite Travis Hunter becoming the first player since Brian Dawkins in 2002 to record a receiving touchdown and an interception in the same game.
Brett, meanwhile, actually managed to win something with Trevor Lawrence this Sunday.
But here's why the Dragons are still #10.
Dubrovnik is averaging 96.4 points per game, with a season high of 123.5.
SIX teams in this league are currently averaging more points than Brett has scored in his BEST week.
His last two victories came against Richmond and a London team that spent the previous week selling Derrick Henry, Tee Higgins and Courtland Sutton.
I'll give Brett full credit for the Hollywood win.
That was a legitimately good performance against Brian.
The other two haven't exactly helped convince me that this roster is ready to compete with the top half of the league.
And the problems are still pretty evident once you get past the young receiving core.

Omarion Hampton is probably one of the bigger RB disappointments so far this year, Dobbins remains one of the few productive veteran assets Brett could realistically sell, and Jaxson Dart is still on IR.
Lawrence accounting for 34 of your 112 points is fantastic when he throws four touchdowns.
I'd be a little concerned about what happens when Jacksonville remembers it also has running backs.
Brett has two first-round picks in 2027, a developing group of young receivers, and now a 3-3 record.
He gets Delco next week, and they just lost Hurts, so extending the streak to 4 is on the table.
12: I tried to find a way to justify moving Darren into third after his win over Jeff.
Unfortunately, Tanish has now led the PDL in scoring for two consecutive weeks, following up last week's 197.72 with another league-high 145.50.

I don't particularly enjoy defending Tanish's roster construction, especially after spending the past month questioning nearly every decision he's made, but he's making it increasingly difficult for me to continue doing so.
I mean, look at his receivers. JSN and Malik Nabers each caught TWELVE passes this weekend, combining for 299 receiving yards without either finding the end zone.
Seattle and the Giants both lost their respective games, but their receivers apparently had an entirely separate agreement to make sure Tanish enjoyed his Sunday.
JSN is currently the WR1 in fantasy, Nabers has looked excellent since returning, and then Tanish was forced to start Charlie White, who contributed zero points on two targets.
Drake Maye continues to look like a legitimate superstar, throwing three more touchdowns against the Jets, while Caleb Williams added another 18.50 points.
Jayden Daniels finished with 25 on the bench, which is a pretty nice luxury to have considering some of the quarterback rooms we've been discussing elsewhere in these rankings.

Jonathan Taylor and Chuba Hubbard also came through, and Tanish managed all of this with Chase Brown on bye, Rashee Rice unavailable, and Dalton Kincaid outscoring his starting tight end from the bench.

Nabers and JSN are doing some extraordinary work to compensate for that third spot, and I'd feel a lot more comfortable about Boulder's championship chances if there were another dependable option available when one of them inevitably has a quiet day.
He's got more than enough running back and quarterback depth to make something happen.
Then again, we're six weeks into the season, the defending champion is 5-1, and he's averaging 153.4 points per game.
Darren absolutely deserves consideration for the top three, especially after knocking off Jeff, but I can't move him ahead of a team that just beat him head-to-head AND outscored him again this week.
Tanish's third receiver scored zero. His third quarterback scored 25.
Please don't let this man propose a rule change.
